disclaimer: Guidance only. Confirm the diagnosis with a local agricultural extension service (in India, your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra) before applying any chemical, and always follow the product label.

bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial spot
bacterial_spot.cause: Xanthomonas spp. (X. euvesicatoria, X. perforans, X. gardneri)
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves, often with a yellow halo
Spots merge and leaves turn yellow and drop
Raised, scabby spots on fruit
management: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Avoid overhead irrigation and handling plants when wet
Rotate away from tomato and pepper for 2–3 years
Copper-based sprays can slow spread; resistance is common

early_blight.name: Early blight
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (a 'target' look) on older, lower leaves
Yellowing around the spots, then leaf drop from the bottom up
Dark, sunken lesions on stems near the soil line
management: Remove infected lower leaves and destroy crop debris
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves
Stake and space plants for airflow; water at the base
Protectant fungicides as advised locally

healthy.name: Healthy
symptoms: Uniform green colour with no spots, mottling or curling
management: Keep scouting weekly, checking both sides of leaves
Water at the base in the morning so foliage dries quickly
Remove weeds and old debris that can harbour pests and disease

late_blight.name: Late blight
symptoms: Large, irregular, greasy grey-green to brown patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth on the underside in humid weather
Firm brown blotches on fruit; can destroy a crop within days
management: Act immediately: remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost)
Avoid leaf wetness; improve spacing and airflow
Use resistant varieties and protectant fungicides as advised locally
Warn nearby growers: it spreads quickly by wind-borne spores

leaf_mold.name: Leaf mould
symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mould on the underside
Mostly in greenhouses and humid, poorly ventilated crops
management: Lower humidity and increase ventilation
Prune and space plants so leaves dry quickly
Remove infected leaves; use resistant varieties

mosaic_virus.name: Tomato mosaic virus
symptoms: Light and dark green mottled (mosaic) pattern on leaves
Distorted, narrow or fern-like leaves
Stunted plants and uneven fruit ripening
management: No cure: remove and destroy infected plants
Spread by hands and tools, so disinfect them between plants
Use certified seed and resistant varieties

septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria leaf spot
symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey-tan centres
Tiny black dots (fruiting bodies) inside the spots
Starts on lower leaves and moves upward
management: Remove infected lower leaves; avoid overhead watering
Mulch and rotate crops; clear debris after harvest
Protectant fungicides as advised locally

spider_mites.name: Two-spotted spider mite
symptoms: Fine yellow or white speckling (stippling) on leaves
Bronzed, dry leaves and fine webbing on the underside
Worse in hot, dry, dusty conditions
management: Check leaf undersides; hose plants down to knock mites off
Protect natural predators: avoid broad-spectrum insecticides
Insecticidal soap, horticultural oil or a labelled miticide

target_spot.name: Target spot
symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and faint concentric rings
Can look like early blight; also affects stems and fruit
Favoured by warm, humid conditions
management: Improve airflow by pruning and spacing
Remove crop debris and rotate crops
Protectant fungicides as advised locally

yellow_leaf_curl_virus.name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
yellow_leaf_curl_virus.cause: TYLCV (begomovirus), spread by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci
symptoms: Leaves curl upward and turn yellow at the edges
Small, crumpled leaves and stunted growth
Flowers drop, so few or no fruit set
management: No cure: remove infected plants early
Control whiteflies with insect-proof nets, yellow sticky traps and reflective mulch
Plant resistant varieties and keep weeds down
